record.paper_title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
record.original_question: For every Tychonoff space X and every infinite subspace S of the closed unit interval [0,1], does the free abelian topological group A(X) admit an open continuous homomorphism onto the free abelian topological group A(S)?

evidence.quote: Let, as usual, F(X) and A(X) denote the free topological group and the free abelian topological group of a Tychonoff space X, respectively.
Does there exist an open continuous homomorphism of A(X) onto A(S), where X is an arbitrary Tychonoff space and S is an infinite subspace of the closed unit interval [0,1]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be an arbitrary Tychonoff (completely regular Hausdorff) topological space, and let A(X) denote its free abelian topological group: the unique (up to topological group isomorphism) abelian Hausdorff topological group containing X as a topological subspace such that X algebraically generates A(X) and every continuous map from X into an abelian Hausdorff topological group G extends uniquely to a continuous group homomorphism A(X) → G. Let S be an infinite subspace of the closed unit interval [0,1] (with its usual topology), and let A(S) be its free abelian topological group.

Question: Does there exist an open continuous group homomorphism from A(X) onto A(S)?

Equivalently, for every Tychonoff space X and every infinite subspace S of [0,1], decide whether A(S) is a topological quotient (in the sense of being the image of an open continuous surjective homomorphism) of A(X).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in a survey on separability of topological groups. Web searches reveal related results on open subgroups and quotients of free abelian topological groups (e.g., work of Morris and Pestov), but no source resolving this specific question about open continuous homomorphisms A(X) → A(S) for arbitrary Tychonoff X and infinite S ⊆ [0,1] was found.

status_evidence.title: Open subgroups of free abelian topological groups
status_evidence.snippet: Every open subgroup of a free Markov (Graev) abelian topological group is a free Markov (respectively, Graev) abelian topological group.
status_evidence.claim: Related structural results exist for open subgroups/quotients but do not resolve the stated question.

status_evidence.title: Open Mapping Theorem for Topological Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Open continuous homomorphisms in topological groups.
status_evidence.claim: General theory on open homomorphisms; no resolution of the specific problem identified.
